clearedSpotChecks.check: The system gcc 13.3 rebuild of the same emitter sources gives the same listing and the same 10,748 hook states as the clang build.
clearedSpotChecks.note: out/asmcmp-gcc13.txt reports 0 differing lines for both gcc listings. The unit's statecmp.py renames every quoted 0x string, which could in principle hide differing values. clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 2 and 3. The package's gcc 15.2.0 Emitter::shl and Emitter::shr on the logged real states of the 12 literal-count shift sites in the 128 un-entered value blocks, including the FullMath.mulDiv blocks, match the clang listing and pyevm.py.
clearedSpotChecks.note: out/model/realshift.json holds per-site gcc and clang streams that I read for three sites (0xf30, 0x21fa, 0x281e). They match up to register renaming. All sites show 0 mismatch runs and 0 clobber runs. faults.log shows six of the planted faults flagged and three not flagged, and the unit says why: no state reaches the spill or variable-count paths. src/libraries/FullMath.sol:47-54 holds the mulmod remainder and the 512-bit subtraction, which have no shift, so the shifts in those blocks come from callers using the FixedPoint96 and FixedPoint128 constants, as the unit's fourth cleared item says. The clearance covers these 12 sites only. The other emit kinds in the same blocks, such as the MUL sites of FullMath.sol:59-91, are still open, and the unit's low-priority lead records that.
